```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 90, digits = 3)
```

```{r setup}
library(bmassa)
```

Are the masses that *bmassa* predicts consistent with masses measured in the
field? Tuesday Lake (Michigan, USA) is one of the few lakes whose whole
pelagic community was described with the mean body mass and the abundance
of every taxon: the phytoplankton, the zooplankton and the fish, sampled in
1984 and in 1986 (Cohen et al. 2003; Jonsson et al. 2005). None of its
masses is in the reference data of *bmassa*, so it is an independent test: if
the prediction intervals are right, about 95 % of the measured masses fall
inside the 95 % intervals, and the biomass of each group inside the interval
of its total.

## The data

The package ships the nodes of the two webs as distributed in the R package
*cheddar* (Hudson et al. 2013; BSD 2-Clause licence): `M` is the mean wet mass
of an individual in kg (in the phytoplankton, of an "algal unit", a cell or
a colony, from its volume) and `N` the individuals per m³.

```{r data}
path <- function(file) system.file("extdata", "tuesday_lake", file, package = "bmassa")
nodes <- read.csv(path("nodes.csv"))
nodes[c(1, 40, 50, 56), ]
table(nodes$year, nodes$category)
```

## Taxa

The names of *cheddar* are cleaned before they are matched: without "sp.",
numbers and the forms in brackets, and with one misspelling corrected
(*Cyclops varians rubellus* for *Cyclops varicans rubellus*, a synonym of
*Microcyclops rubellus*). The unclassified flagellates have no taxon and are
left out.

```{r names}
clean_name <- function(x) {
  x <- sub("-spiny", "", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- sub(" \\((solitary|colonial)\\)$", "", x)
  x <- sub(" sp\\. ?[0-9]*$", "", x)
  x[grepl("^Unclassified", x)] <- NA_character_
  x[x == "Cyclops varians rubellus"] <- "Microcyclops rubellus"
  x
}
units <- nodes[!duplicated(nodes$node), c("node", "category", "family")]
units$taxon_id <- units$node
units$broad_group <- c(producer = "phytoplankton", invertebrate = "zooplankton",
                       vert.ecto = "fish")[units$category]
units$scientific_name <- clean_name(units$node)
units <- units[!is.na(units$scientific_name), ]
```

`standardize_taxa()` gives the classification of the Catalogue of Life, with
the family of *cheddar* as a hint for homonyms. It needs internet, so the
vignette reads its result (run on 2026-11-07):

```{r standardize, eval = FALSE}
taxa <- standardize_taxa(units[c("taxon_id", "broad_group", "scientific_name", "family")])
```

```{r standardize-stored}
taxa <- read.csv(path("taxa.csv"), colClasses = "character")
taxa[!is.na(taxa$note), c("scientific_name", "col_name", "match_type")][1:6, ]
```

```{r check-stored, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(taxa$taxon_id, units$taxon_id),
          identical(taxa$scientific_name, units$scientific_name))
```

Jonsson et al. (2005) measured the phytoplankton per algal unit, so it is
counted in natural units; *Chaoborus* are larvae. Nothing else is known
about the stages: the copepods are therefore taken as adults.

```{r taxa}
taxa$count_unit <- ifelse(taxa$broad_group == "phytoplankton", "natural_unit", "individual")
taxa$life_stage <- ifelse(taxa$genus %in% "Chaoborus", "larva", NA_character_)
taxa$group <- ifelse(taxa$broad_group != "zooplankton", taxa$broad_group,
              ifelse(taxa$phylum %in% "Rotifera", "rotifers",
              ifelse(taxa$class %in% "Branchiopoda", "cladocerans",
              ifelse(taxa$class %in% "Copepoda", "copepods", "Chaoborus"))))
table(taxa$group)
```

## Masses: measured against predicted

The abundances per m³ of each year, and the mean mass of every taxon in
wet mass, in µg, without lengths:

```{r estimate}
ab <- nodes[nodes$node %in% taxa$taxon_id, ]
ab <- data.frame(site = as.character(ab$year), taxon_id = ab$node, abundance = ab$N_m3, per = "m3",
                 M_ug = ab$M_kg * 1e9)
ab$group <- taxa$group[match(ab$taxon_id, taxa$taxon_id)]
est <- estimate_biomass(ab, taxa, unit = "ug")
est
```

The colonies of *Conochilus* measured in 1986 are compared with nothing:
*bmassa* estimates individuals.

```{r inside}
e <- as.data.frame(est)
e <- e[e$taxon_id != "Conochilus (colonial)", ]
e$inside <- e$M_ug >= e$ind_lower & e$M_ug <= e$ind_upper
e$ratio <- e$ind_median / e$M_ug
groups <- c("phytoplankton", "rotifers", "cladocerans", "copepods", "Chaoborus", "fish")
cover <- do.call(rbind, lapply(groups, function(g) {
  s <- e[e$group == g, ]
  data.frame(group = g, compared = nrow(s), inside_95 = mean(s$inside),
             median_ratio = stats::median(s$ratio),
             width_95 = stats::median(s$ind_upper / s$ind_lower))
}))
cover
c(compared = nrow(e), inside_95 = mean(e$inside))
```

`inside_95` is the share of the measured masses inside the 95 % prediction
interval, `median_ratio` the median of predicted over measured, and
`width_95` the median ratio of the upper to the lower limit. About nine in
ten measured masses fall inside the intervals. The intervals are wide,
because without lengths a taxon is predicted from the typical masses of its
species or relatives: they say how much a mass of an unmeasured population
can differ from the typical one.

```{r plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Measured mean individual mass of each taxon of Tuesday Lake against the median predicted by bmassa, in µg on log scales, with the 95 % prediction intervals; most points lie close to the line of equality and inside their intervals"}
col <- c(phytoplankton = "#1b9e77", rotifers = "#d95f02", cladocerans = "#7570b3",
         copepods = "#e7298a", Chaoborus = "#66a61e", fish = "#a6761d")
op <- par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
plot(e$M_ug, e$ind_median, log = "xy", pch = 19, col = col[e$group],
     xlim = range(e$M_ug, e$ind_lower, e$ind_upper), ylim = range(e$ind_lower, e$ind_upper),
     xlab = "Measured mean mass (µg)", ylab = "Predicted mean mass (µg)")
segments(e$M_ug, e$ind_lower, e$M_ug, e$ind_upper, col = col[e$group])
abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
legend("topleft", names(col), col = col, pch = 19, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
par(op)
```

The masses outside their intervals:

```{r outside}
out <- e[!e$inside, c("site", "taxon_id", "group", "M_ug", "ind_median", "ind_lower",
                      "ind_upper", "match_level")]
out[order(abs(log(out$ind_median / out$M_ug)), decreasing = TRUE), ]
```

Most are colonial algae (*Chrysosphaerella*, *Dinobryon*, *Gloeocystis*,
*Synedra*), measured whole, whose natural units in the reference are single
cells or small groups: `cells_per_unit` in `taxa` gives the cells of a
colony counted whole. The *Keratella* are predicted heavier than measured,
like the rotifers in general, and the copepods about twice as heavy: taken
as adults, a count that includes copepodites is overestimated (as
copepodites, with `life_stage = "copepodite"`, most come out lighter than
measured, and their measured means lie between the two). The largemouth bass
of 1986, introduced adults, are much heavier than the fish of the reference
without lengths.

## Biomass: measured against predicted totals

The biomass of each group, the sum of `M × N` over its taxa, against the
total of *bmassa* for the same taxa, whose interval keeps the correlations
between the taxa estimated from the same relatives:

```{r totals}
tot <- summarize_biomass(est, by = c("site", "group"), na_rm = TRUE, n_draws = 10000, seed = 1)
measured <- stats::aggregate(B ~ site + group, data = transform(e, B = M_ug * abundance), FUN = sum)
tot <- merge(tot[, c("site", "group", "biomass_unit", "biomass_median", "biomass_lower",
                     "biomass_upper")], measured, by = c("site", "group"))
tot$inside <- tot$B >= tot$biomass_lower & tot$B <= tot$biomass_upper
tot[, c("site", "group", "B", "biomass_median", "biomass_lower", "biomass_upper", "inside")]
```

The measured biomass of every group falls inside the interval of its total
in both years, except that of the fish in 1986, the bass. The intervals of
the totals are narrower, relative to the estimate, than those of single taxa
when the group has many taxa with independent errors (the phytoplankton), and
as wide when one taxon makes the group (*Chaoborus*).

- Jonsson T, Cohen JE, Carpenter SR (2005). Food webs, body size, and
